llm_utils.py¶

In [2]:
!cat llm_utils.py

import time, json
from datetime import datetime
import config

PROMPTS = {
 "v1": "Answer the following student question clearly.\nQuestion: {{question}}",
 "v2": ("You are an academic assistant.\nAnswer the following student question in a clear, "
        "concise, and accurate manner.\nUse simple language suitable for undergraduate students.\n"
        "Question: {{question}}"),
 "v3": ("You are an academic assistant.\nAnswer the student question and return ONLY valid JSON.\n"
        "Do not include markdown, explanations outside JSON, or code fences.\nUse this exact JSON schema:\n"
        "{\n  \"answer\": \"string\",\n  \"confidence\": \"high | medium | low\",\n  \"key_points\": [\"string\"]\n}\n"
        "Question: {{question}}"),
}

def cost(in_tok, out_tok):
    ic = in_tok / 1e6 * config.INPUT_PRICE_PER_M
    oc = out_tok / 1e6 * config.OUTPUT_PRICE_PER_M
    return ic, oc, ic + oc

def is_valid_json(text):
    try:
        d = json.loads(text)
        return isinstance(d, dict) and {"answer", "confidence", "key_points"} <= d.keys()
    except Exception:
        return False

def ask(qid, question, version, template):
    prompt = template.replace("{{question}}", question)
    row = {"question_id": qid, "prompt_version": version, "model": config.MODEL,
           "start_time": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")}
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        r = config.client.chat.completions.create(model=config.MODEL,
              messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=1024, temperature=0)
        text, in_tok, out_tok, status = (r.choices[0].message.content or "",
              r.usage.prompt_tokens, r.usage.completion_tokens, "success")
    except Exception as e:
        text, in_tok, out_tok, status = "", 0, 0, f"error: {type(e).__name__}"
    lat = time.perf_counter() - t0
    row["end_time"] = datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")
    ic, oc, tc = cost(in_tok, out_tok)
    row.update({"latency_seconds": round(lat, 3), "status": status,
                "input_tokens": in_tok, "output_tokens": out_tok, "total_tokens": in_tok + out_tok,
                "input_cost_usd": ic, "output_cost_usd": oc, "total_cost_usd": tc,
                "valid_json": is_valid_json(text), "response": text})
    return row

Interpretation. All 5 requests succeeded. Mean latency was 1.214 s (median 1.213 s) with a small spread (std 0.132 s, range 1.007-1.333 s). The slowest request was Q5 ("Explain gradient descent in simple terms", 1.333 s). It also produced the most output tokens (171). An LLM generates its answer one token at a time, so longer, more explanatory answers take longer, and "explain in simple terms" invites a longer answer. Token count is not the whole story, though. Q3 generated only 115 tokens yet took 1.325 s, while Q1 generated 168 tokens in 1.213 s. With answers this short, network round-trip and server-side queueing on a shared, free-tier endpoint add jitter of about 0.1-0.3 s, which is as large as the effect of answer length. With only 5 samples these figures are indicative; production monitoring should track p95/p99 latency over many requests.

Task 2 - Token Usage and Cost Estimation¶

Input Cost = input_tokens / 1,000,000 x 0.30 USD; Output Cost = output_tokens / 1,000,000 x 2.50 USD; Total = Input + Output; Projected monthly cost = average cost per request x 10,000 requests.

avg = df1["total_cost_usd"].mean()
out_share = df1["output_cost_usd"].sum() / df1["total_cost_usd"].sum()
print(f"Average cost per request : ${avg:.8f}")

Average cost per request : $0.00037366
Projected monthly cost   : $3.7366  (10,000 requests/month, USD)
Share of cost from output tokens: 93.0%

Cost-optimisation recommendation. Output tokens cause about 93% of the cost: they are 8.3x more expensive than input tokens, and the model writes more than it reads. The most effective lever is therefore to limit the answer length. Add a length rule to the production prompt, such as "answer in at most 80 words and give at most 3 key_points", and set max_tokens to around 250 as a safety cap. Cutting the average output from about 139 to about 70 tokens would lower cost per request by about 46%, and it would also reduce latency, because generation time grows with output length. Repeated questions (for example common course FAQs) could additionally be served from a response cache, which avoids an API call altogether.

Task 3 - Prompt Versioning and Evaluation with MLflow¶

3.1 Register prompts v1, v2, v3 in the MLflow Prompt Registry¶

In [8]:
NAME = "eduassist_prompt"
MSG = {"v1": "v1: baseline - minimal instruction, free-text answer",
       "v2": "v2: add academic-assistant role, clarity and undergraduate-level language",
       "v3": "v3: enforce strict JSON output schema (answer, confidence, key_points), no markdown"}
try:
    mlflow.genai.load_prompt(f"prompts:/{NAME}/3"); print("prompt versions already registered - skipping")
except Exception:
    for v in ["v1", "v2", "v3"]:
        p = mlflow.genai.register_prompt(name=NAME, template=PROMPTS[v], commit_message=MSG[v],
                                         tags={"label": v, "app": "EduAssist"})
        print("registered", NAME, "version", p.version)
for ver in [1, 2, 3]:
    p = mlflow.genai.load_prompt(f"prompts:/{NAME}/{ver}")
    print(f"\n--- version {p.version} | commit: {p.commit_message}\n{p.template}")

3.3 Evaluation runs¶

valid_json = responses that parse as JSON with keys answer, confidence, key_points / total responses.

In [10]:
mlflow.set_experiment("eduassist_llmops_assignment")
existing = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["eduassist_llmops_assignment"])
if RERUN or len(existing) < 3:
    summary, details = [], []
    for ver in [1, 2, 3]:
        p = mlflow.genai.load_prompt(f"prompts:/{NAME}/{ver}"); label = f"v{ver}"
        df = pd.DataFrame([ask(qid, q, label, p.template) for qid, q in config.QUESTIONS.items()])
        details += df.to_dict("records")
        m = {"avg_latency_seconds": df.latency_seconds.mean(), "avg_input_tokens": df.input_tokens.mean(),
             "avg_output_tokens": df.output_tokens.mean(), "avg_cost_per_request": df.total_cost_usd.mean(),
             "valid_json": df.valid_json.mean()}
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"prompt_{label}"):
            mlflow.log_params({"prompt_name": NAME, "prompt_version": ver, "prompt_uri": f"prompts:/{NAME}/{ver}",
                               "model": config.MODEL, "api": config.API_STYLE, "temperature": 0,
                               "n_questions": len(df), "price_in_per_1M_usd": config.INPUT_PRICE_PER_M,
                               "price_out_per_1M_usd": config.OUTPUT_PRICE_PER_M, "pricing_date": config.PRICE_DATE})
            mlflow.log_metrics(m)
            mlflow.log_table(df, artifact_file=f"responses_{label}.json")
        summary.append({"version": label, **m})
    pd.DataFrame(summary).to_csv("prompt_evaluation_results.csv", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(details).to_csv("prompt_evaluation_details.csv", index=False)
else:
    print("using the 3 runs already logged in MLflow")

3.5 Promote the best version with the alias production¶

In [13]:
mlflow.genai.set_prompt_alias(NAME, alias="production", version=int(best[1:]))
p = mlflow.genai.load_prompt(f"prompts:/{NAME}@production")
print(f"prompts:/{NAME}@production -> version {p.version} ({p.commit_message})")

prompts:/eduassist_prompt@production -> version 3 (v3: enforce strict JSON output schema (answer, confidence, key_points), no markdown)

Promotion justification¶

Version 3 was promoted to production because it is the only version that meets the EduAssist product requirement and it is also the most efficient. The application expects a machine-readable JSON object with answer, confidence and key_points. v3 produced valid JSON for 5 of 5 questions (100%), while v1 and v2 returned free-form text and scored 0%, so their output would break the downstream parser no matter how good the content is.

v3 is also the best on cost and latency. Its prompt is the longest (87.2 input tokens versus 22.2 for v1), but the fixed schema keeps the model's answers short: 149.4 output tokens on average versus 461.8 for v1 and 308.4 for v2. Output tokens are priced 8.3x higher than input tokens, so v3 costs USD 0.000400 per request, which is 66% cheaper than v1 (USD 0.001161) and 49% cheaper than v2 (USD 0.000785). At 10,000 requests a month that is about USD 4.00 versus USD 11.61 for v1. Shorter generation also halves latency, from 2.18 s for v1 to 1.10 s.

The trade-off is that v3's answers are more condensed than v2's explanatory text, and confidence is self-reported by the model. Using a registry alias means the application loads prompts:/eduassist_prompt@production, so a future v4 can be promoted, or v3 rolled back, by moving the alias without any code change.

Conclusion¶

gemini-3.5-flash-lite answered the 5 academic questions in about 1.2 s each, at about USD 0.00037 per request (about USD 3.74 per month for 10,000 requests). Prompt versioning in MLflow showed that the prompt with the strict JSON schema (v3) is the most reliable, cheapest and fastest, and it now serves as the production alias.
